Chapter 9: Navigating Setbacks and Sustaining Progress
Healing, as you’ve probably noticed by now, is almost never a straight path. There’ll be days when old symptoms sneak back in, new challenges pop up, or you just feel like you’re moving at a snail’s pace.
Navigating these ups and downs with patience and a good dose of self-compassion makes all the difference when it comes to long-term well-being.
Think about setbacks like the changing seasons in a garden. Sometimes, there’s growth and color everywhere—other times, things slow down and go quiet for a while. That doesn’t mean you’ve failed. In fact, these pauses can be a chance to go back to your roots, revisit the basics, and build an even stronger foundation.
So, how can you move through these tougher moments? Here are a few things that really help:
First, return to the essentials. Pick up those core practices that always support you—like affirmations, mindfulness, or your favorite self-care routines.
Next, don’t be afraid to reach out. Whether it’s a trusted friend, a professional, or a support group, sharing what you’re going through can offer encouragement and a new perspective.
Remember to practice self-forgiveness, too. Let go of the self-blame and recognize the effort you’re putting in—even if things aren’t perfect.
And don’t overlook the little victories. Sometimes, the smallest improvements or insights are worth celebrating.
Here’s something else to keep in mind: healing is shaped by many different factors, and not all of them are in your control. Maybe it’s outside stress, a big life transition, or a shift in your health. When things change, it’s OK to adjust your routines and expectations. Flexibility and adaptability really are your best allies.
By approaching setbacks with curiosity and kindness, you give yourself the chance to learn and keep moving forward. Every challenge is an opportunity to build resilience and recommit to your well-being.
So, the next time things feel tough, remember—you’re still growing, even if it doesn’t look like it on the surface.
